critiques.description: Most of the previous round's BLOCKING MUST-FIX items are still unaddressed, even though the corrected material now exists on disk twice. (1) The iter-3 hypothesis update (iter_3/upd_hypo/.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json §0 'CORRECTED RECORD OF ITERATION 3') restates every iter-3 number with its source and tells the paper step to transcribe it. (2) gen_art_evaluation_3 (art_BvAL_KZTZuw8) Part 4 writes the correction tables: tables/hypothesis_verdicts_iter3.csv (T1(c) 'SIG PASS / FREE NOT_TESTABLE, so NOT CONFIRMED'; T1(e) rename invariance FAILED; M3 INCONCLUSIVE, since the specifications conflict; NET degrades; typing negative), perturb_corrected.csv, rename_selection_dead_end.csv, t2_record.csv, cost_units.csv, coverage_vs_request_iter3.csv, function_inventory.csv, label_facts.csv, corrections_iter12.csv, artifact_id_map.csv and prior_art.csv. The report used only the C8 cost correction and the per-sentence k-costs (§4.6). Still wrong or missing: §3.4 still calls MEANING_RENAME 'the false-alarm diagnostic … meaning-preserving' and still ranks operators by consensus AUROC, and T3 still claims 'polarity-symmetric'. §3.3 and §3.6 item 3 still record T2 as CONFIRMED. §3.5 still redefines M1/M2 (M1 'not formally tested'; M2 as the e/d bookkeeping identity) and still gives the M4 cost column as $0.000024–0.000170 'per sentence', which contradicts §4.6's own $0.000315–0.002206 per sentence. §3.2–3.6 still cite placeholder IDs [ARTIFACT:art_T1_API_bar], art_R_COMP, art_PERTURB_scoring and art_evaluation_2 (the real IDs are in artifact_id_map.csv). E is still called 'held-out' in the iter-3 text and in 'What we have learned'. There is still no section and no marker for the research artifact art_VIF75I5R6f0v. The iter-1/iter-2 correction items (1)–(9) are still unapplied, e.g. §1.4/§1.5 frontier '+0.024 … adds nothing' vs C4, §2.5 item 5 'reversing', '588 common items', 'fitted under solver labels'. §3.1 still has no reasoning block. There is no coverage table, no function inventory, no Part C typing table and no rename-selection dead end. §3.6 still says iter-3 spend was '$1.58 plus T1', but §4.6 says $4.33. critiques.description: §4.2 (exp 9, art_D7k2ZWgE3nVd) has numbers that do not match the artifact, and gates that are misdefined. I recomputed from results/per_item_csc_E.jsonl (audit/recompute_csc.py/.json). The points reproduce: n 354/196, c_csc strat 0.6136, FREE_exact 0.7697, c_score_align 0.774, e 0.459/0.173, d 0.139/0.323. My sentence-cluster CI for c_csc is [0.501, 0.728], which matches tables.md T4 [0.493, 0.736]. MISMATCHES: (a) every CI in the headline AUROC table is narrower than the source. c_csc: report [0.545, 0.679] vs file [0.493, 0.736]; p_peer_text [0.742, 0.848] vs [0.700, 0.880]; c_score_align [0.711, 0.827] vs [0.682, 0.857]; FREE_exact [0.704, 0.827] vs [0.686, 0.844]; S4_full [0.672, 0.791] vs [0.635, 0.826]; flash-lite [0.592, 0.731] vs [0.568, 0.750]. (b) 'Anchoring by error class' COMPOUND e_CSC 0.643 / e_FREE_exact 0.246. T9 gives 0.282 [0.182, 0.382] / 0.107; 0.643 is the pooled CSC_graded e. With the correct value, COMPOUND is among the LEAST anchored classes, which undercuts the report's reading. (c) The M3 interaction −0.232 [−0.417, −0.041]. T13 gives [−0.770, −0.023], and the stacked-GEE spec −0.351 [−0.694, −0.009] is omitted. (d) The gates are misdefined. prereg_csc_E.json has G2 = 'strat AUROC(CSC) ≥ c_score_align − 0.01 AND pooled AUROC(CSC) > c_score_align on L25'; the report writes it as 'strat AUROC ≥ 0.700'. csc_gate_E.json marks G2 R_AB-part FAIL and L25 NOT_READ, so the overall verdict is NOT_READ, not a plain FAIL. G3-E is the RENAME_SYN false-alarm gate (NOT_RUN); the report calls it 'E2 confirmation'. (e) The 'NET summary' says CSC 'degrades … relative to the FREE baseline'. NET is the within-arm change from word tercile T1 to T3 (T3b); the FREE arms degrade too (FULL FREE_exact +0.452, FREE_align +0.401). (f) 'CSC is below … the flash-lite judge (0.664)' is not significant: the paired Δ is −0.050 [−0.212, +0.107] (T5), and CSC vs S4_full is −0.123 [−0.269, +0.010].
critiques.suggested_action: Re-transcribe §4.2 from exp 9 tables.md T0–T17 and csc_gate_E.json, with CIs copied verbatim. Fix COMPOUND to 0.282/0.107 and add the full T9 and T9b tables. Replace the gate descriptions with the prereg text and G2 = NOT_READ (R_AB part FAIL). Give M3 under both specifications. Reword NET as length degradation within each arm. State that CSC vs flash-lite and vs S4_full are n.s. on PRIMARY.

critiques.description: §4.2 leaves out the facts needed to judge the CSC negative result, and its framing overstates the anchoring mechanism. (1) PRIMARY is a completion-selected subset, not a random one. CTRL makes up 44.9% of its CORRECT rows vs 27.4% on FULL (recomputed), and no stratum reaches 50/50, so L25, the user's priority stratum, is NOT_READ. c_csc is almost binary (tie rate 0.986). The prereg calls the gate PROVISIONAL; the report calls CSC 'a dead end'. (2) The MEANING_RENAME contrast '0.821 vs 0.036' is taken against FREE_exact. Against FREE_ALIGN, the aligner that c_score_align itself uses, e is already 0.750, and Δ CSC − FREE_ALIGN is +0.071 [−0.083, +0.269] (NOT_READ). So aligner-based consensus endorses these errors almost as often as CSC does. On FULL, FREE_ALIGN e on MEANING_RENAME-type errors is 0.624 (T9b). (3) Omitted results: the HYB_MEAN arm (strat 0.709, fails G1); T8, where only 20.2% of CORRECT rows flagged by free-exact have every disagreement vocabulary-resolvable and 53% of disagreements are structural; T10 typing (own_majority 0.185, below the majority class 0.262); T14 system-level τ (CSC 0.256, p = 0.25); T17 phi-4 exemplar leakage (58 CSC calls copied the few-shot exemplar; the clean c_csc is 0.639, and Δ vs FREE_exact clean is −0.132 [−0.251, −0.023]); T15, the 9-peer c_score_align rename ΔFA +0.273 [+0.164, +0.384] under WordNet synonyms; the T2 FULL e/d (FREE_exact d 0.583); the deviations; and G5, whose deduped cost is $2.76e-4.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a 'Population and selection' paragraph (T0, T0b, tie rate, PROVISIONAL status). Replace the anchoring sentence with the FREE_exact and FREE_ALIGN columns side by side. Add T8, T10, T14, T15 and T17 as tables with their source paths, plus the HYB_MEAN row. Downgrade 'dead end' to 'provisional negative on a completion-selected subset; L25 and RENAME untested'.

critiques.description: §4.3 (exp 10, art_pAmLrGqsmFUx) draws a conclusion its own tables contradict. 'FREE consensus achieves near-perfect recall on PERTURB (e ≈ 0, recall ≈ 1.0)' leaves out the matching false-alarm rate on the verified-CORRECT bases (T4). I recomputed from results/perturb_csc_scores.jsonl (audit/recompute_perturb_csc.json). Base FA at c > 0.5 is 0.712 for c_align_exp8 on E, 0.803 for FREE3_exact on E, 0.986 for FREE3_exact on R_COMP and 0.757 for FREE3_align on R_COMP, with mutant recall 0.998–1.000 in every case. A score that flags 71–99% of verified-correct formulas has trivial recall. The same problem affects 'All consensus variants flag RENAME controls at 85–100% FA': the paired flip rates are 0.18–0.53 (c_align E SYN 0.182, NONCE 0.327). The report omits them, so most of that FA is base FA. Other misreadings: (a) LOCAL2 e 0.341 is read as 'weaker models failing to distinguish mutants'. Every one of those endorsements is an insufficient-peer tie at c = 0.5 (share exactly 0.5 = 0.341, recomputed; T3 e_excl_insufficient 0.012/0.007). (b) The judge's 12.4% mutant miss rate is said to be 'matching the iteration-3 E endorsement rate', but that 0.124 is END_MAJ e on real errors, a different quantity. (c) Typing: 'oracle' repairs against the known gold base, so it is not a gold-free metric. free3 on E is 0.123 [0.081, 0.169]; the report gives the pooled 0.085, which includes R_COMP rows at 0.0. (d) The controls table mixes sources: FREE3_exact REORDER/CONTRA 0.986 is R_COMP, while the E values are 0.842/0.840. (e) T4 (d rises with length: c_align 0.47/0.80/0.91 by tercile) and T8 (R_COMP FREE label-free agreement, ALIGN 0.219) are omitted.
critiques.suggested_action: Add T4 (d on bases) next to every recall figure and state plainly that FREE consensus recall ≈ 1 comes with base FA 0.71–0.99. Add the paired base FA and flip columns from T5. Correct the LOCAL2, judge-12.4% and typing sentences as above, and label the oracle as gold-using. Split the controls table by base_source.

critiques.description: §4.6 and 'What we have learned' misread eval 3 (art_BvAL_KZTZuw8). (1) 'The predicted d_floor (0.402) closely matches the observed END_MAJ d (0.415), indicating that the Part-1 model accounts for the observed disagreement.' The artifact says the reverse. The instrument bracket is [0.396, 0.415], the pre-registered gap_closed rule is ill-conditioned (denominator 0.013), and the instruments 'cannot see most vocabulary divergence'. (2) 'R_exact AUROC (0.683) is the theoretical performance of cross-family exact-match consensus on R_COMP under independent vocabulary.' 0.683 is d under the exact rule on E's 3-pool (tables/p1_rule_cuts.csv); it is not an AUROC and not R_COMP. 'What we have learned' then repeats 'R_COMP FREE d_floor 0.402, theoretical AUROC 0.683'. Both numbers are E quantities, and neither is an AUROC. (3) The calibration failure is attributed to 'vocabulary-driven non-transitivity'. The artifact says predicted FREE endorsement 0.20 vs actual SIG 0.575, i.e. the instruments under-count vocabulary effects, and D7 notes that SIG changes granularity and structure as well, so the SIG−FREE drop is an upper bound. Non-transitivity (0.131) is a separate diagnostic. (4) Omitted: 77% (9-family) and 61% (3-pool) of the non-agreeing peers of CORRECT candidates are labelled ERROR, so d is mostly peer error, not vocabulary; pair classes (IRREDUCIBLE 69.4%); the specificity placebo (VOCAB agreements are not label-specific); c_vres L25 −0.014 [−0.028, −0.001]; NET DEGRADES under every rule (+0.35 to +0.39); the no-anchoring oracle floor 0.385 and L25 0.542 vs 0.735; SIG row endorsement 0.575 vs FREE 0.193; the p3 power grid (L25 250–400 → MDE 0.130–0.103, all MARGINAL); R_COMP FREE needs ≥ 200 CORRECT rows; deviations D1–D10; the reusable functions table.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite §4.6 from the eval-3 README 'Results in one table' and 'What this means' sections, row for row with source paths. Delete 'closely matches … accounts for' and the '0.683 theoretical AUROC on R_COMP' wording in both §4.6 and 'What we have learned', and replace them with 'the post-hoc instruments predict almost no fix and are shown to under-count vocabulary effects (calibration error −0.372)'. Add the 77%/61% peer-labelled-ERROR decomposition as the main mechanism finding.

critiques.description: §4.4 and §4.5 (datasets 4 and 5) drop caveats that change how the data should be read, and §3.3 now has results computed on labels this iteration invalidated. E2 (art_2OmxzMInZZJY): the report says the gate balanced accuracies 'all pass'. panel_drift_E2.json says the stop rule is 'UNDECIDED', with passes = false and combined majority agreement 0.394 over all items. On the 22 replayed unambiguous track-H judgements, today's panel flags only 0.12 of original errors vs 0.84 in E (orig_flagged_rate_unamb). That is a drift warning, small n, and it is not recorded. Deviations D0–D7 (including D1, ProverQA gold under the MALLS audit shim, and D4, re-issued phi-4 calls) are not listed. The label recount I did matches: 36 ERROR / 274 UNRESOLVED / 20 UNPARSEABLE / 0 CORRECT. R_COMP FREE (art_Ia_FT284H33j): the counts reproduce (759/1,506/188/199). But '70.7% contaminated' treats MAPPED as CORRECT, while the artifact calls MAPPED an upper bound (executor audit: 0.867 faithful). The disagreement sample includes a MAPPED certificate that swaps LivesIn and StudentInClass, i.e. a real error passing the search. Also omitted: old/new kappa 0.058; rescue rate by template (T8 0.27, T9 0.37–0.43); deviations D1–D9, including D6, which amends the map family after the freeze. Most importantly, §3.3's FREE numbers (c_align − judge +0.214; 'falls to ~0.80') were computed on the iter-3 FREE tier-A labels that this artifact shows to be mostly wrong, and §3.3 carries no in-place correction.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the drift stop-rule status and the 0.12-vs-0.84 track-H signal to §4.4, with the deviations list. Word §4.5 as 'up to 70.7% (MAPPED is an upper bound; 13% of MAPPED unfaithful in audit)', and add kappa, rescue-by-template and the deviations. Insert '[Correction, iter 4: FREE tier-A labels shown to over-call ERROR (297/420 MAPPED); the FREE deltas in this section are void; source gen_art_dataset_5/results/old_label_agreement.json]' into §3.3.

critiques.description: Iteration 4 spent its budget on a new metric variant (CSC) and a CPU-side mechanism analysis over a panel its own power analysis calls underpowered. It did not spend it on the graded samples that would decide the question. eval-3 power_E2.json: L25 yield 0.37; detecting the observed +0.069 needs ~882 planned L25 sentences; E2's 350 give MDE80 0.112 and power 0.32–0.47. R_COMP FREE needs ≥ 200 CORRECT rows. Against the user's request, the new section adds no testable result on long, heavily conditioned sentences: CSC L25 is NOT_READ, E2 has 0 CORRECT rows, and R_COMP FREE has an empty CORRECT class. The operating condition 'no ontology or controlled vocabulary' is still unvalidated: the only positive new numbers (SIGPROXY 0.930; d 0.149) come from the signature-given regime the user put out of scope. 'Which kind of error' is again negative outside shared vocabulary (free3 typing 0.123 on E, ≈ the judge). The report does not state any of these as answers to the request, and 'What remains' ranks completing E2 and the gloss together with more CSC arms.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the 'Coverage against the request' table (start from coverage_vs_request_iter3.csv and update it with iter-4 rows), with explicit one-line answers: long sentences → untested in iter 4; no-controlled-vocabulary → consensus unvalidated (FREE untestable); error type → negative. In 'What remains', rank first the R_COMP FREE gloss (~$1.8, gives CORRECT labels in the in-scope condition) and E2 completion sized to ≥ 237 usable long-pool sentences with the long pool pre-declared primary. Drop the remaining CSC PERTURB arms until those have run.

critiques.description: §4.1 records what iteration 4 did but not why. It omits: the previous review (score 3, blocking, 12 items) and which of those objections iteration 4 set out to answer (eval-3 Part 4 was built for this, and the report does not say so); the iter-3 upd_hypo decision (move = DEEPEN; title 'Peer agreement in the candidate's own words'; the §0 corrected record); the prediction CSC was meant to test (a lower d without a higher e, with eval 3's pre-registered d_floor prediction as the yardstick) and the stopping rule; the five planned artifacts with their planned vs actual spend. The budget event is described three different ways ('budget event at $0.108', 'run-wide budget ($7.00) exhausted by earlier artifacts', 'exhausted at 07:26 UTC') and never reconciled into a spend table. Summing the ledgers gives exp 9 $0.108, exp 10 $0.0000088, dataset 4 $0.241, dataset 5 $0 and eval 3 $0, about $0.35 in total. That leaves most of the $7 'Test idea' budget spent by something the report never names.
critiques.suggested_action: Open §4 with an 8–10 line reasoning block drawn from iter_3/upd_hypo and iter_4/gen_strat/gen_strat_1: the previous review score and blocking status, the move, the CSC prediction and gate definitions, the artifacts planned. Add an iter-4 spend table from each artifact's cost ledger, and say which process consumed the run budget before 07:26.

critiques.description: The iteration's positive claims have no nearest-neighbour check, and the research artifact still has no section. The claims are 'Vocabulary sharing reduces d by 0.61–0.84 while maintaining perfect mutant recall' and 'Error typing requires shared vocabulary'. Supplying a predicate list is a documented lever for NL→FOL: Vossel et al. 2025 (arXiv 2509.22338, cited as [24]) report that 'predicate availability boosts performance by 15–20%'. ARc (2511.09008, [19]) scores translations over a fixed shared schema precisely so that k translations can be compared. What SIGPROXY adds is a measured d reduction on long templated sentences in an out-of-scope controlled-vocabulary regime, and the record should say only that. The anchoring finding (peers given the candidate's symbols copy its errors) is the correlated-failure mode the report itself cites from Chen & Avizienis [25]. Its new element is the per-class e measurement, but the MEANING_RENAME contrast shrinks to +0.071 n.s. against the aligner baseline. art_VIF75I5R6f0v still has no [ARTIFACT] marker, no scoop-rule statement and no C1–C5 verdict table, although eval 3 exports prior_art.csv for exactly this.
critiques.suggested_action: Add '3.x Prior-art positioning [ARTIFACT:art_VIF75I5R6f0v]' (scoop rule, closest-neighbour table, C1–C5 verdicts with qualifiers, from prior_art.csv). Under §4.3's shared-vocabulary claim and §4.2's anchoring claim, add one sentence each naming Vossel/ARc and Chen & Avizienis, and saying what the measurement adds.
